:::{#exr-hyperplane-subspace-practice}
#### Checking that a normal vector is orthogonal to a hyperplane

Part 3 of @thm-hyperplane-subspace says that,
for a [hyperplane](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-hyperplane),
its [normal vector](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-normal-vector) is [orthogonal](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-orthogonal-vectors)
to the difference of any two of its points.
Let $\mathcal{H} = \cb{\vx \in \reals^3 : 2 x_1 - x_2 + x_3 - 4 = 0}$,
with normal vector $\vec{w} = (2, -1, 1)$.
The points $\vx = (2, 0, 0)$ and $\vy = (0, 0, 4)$ are both in $\mathcal{H}$.

Check that $\vec{w} \cdot (\vx - \vy) = 0$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Compute $\vx - \vy$ first.

:::

:::
